overview: This atlas record begins in 1945, but the United Arab Emirates did not exist until 2 December 1971. Before then, the same map bucket covers the British-protected Trucial sheikhdoms; the separate imported record trucial-oman-1938 ends at 1945. Five broad polygon snapshots run only through 2020 even though the lifetime is open. Point tests put Dubai, Sharjah, Fujairah and Al Ain inside the 1945 shape, but Abu Dhabi, Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Ras Al Khaimah outside it, while the western edge sweeps far into modern Saudi-border space. Treat it as an approximate display area, never a legal border. Ancient Al Ain discoveries below are labeled antecedents, not accomplishments of the modern federation.

periods.title: Trucial sheikhdoms under British protection
periods.summary: Across this interval, the coastal Trucial sheikhdoms were linked to Britain by treaty; the atlas applies the later federal name before the federation existed.

periods.title: Federation founded, then completed
periods.summary: Six emirates formed the UAE on 2 December 1971; Ras Al Khaimah became the seventh on 10 February 1972.

periods.title: Oil-funded development and federal consolidation
periods.summary: Oil income supported rapid construction and public services while substantial authority remained with the individual emirates.

periods.title: Partial FNC elections and consultation
periods.summary: The federation expanded electoral-college selection for half of the advisory Federal National Council while rulers continued to appoint the other half.

periods.title: Mohamed bin Zayed presidency
periods.summary: The seven-ruler Federal Supreme Council elected Mohamed bin Zayed president in May 2022, continuing the federal monarchy.

sections.title: From protected sheikhdoms to a federation

items.text: In 1945 there was no country called the United Arab Emirates. The coastal polities in this record were Trucial sheikhdoms under British protection; by federation there were seven: Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Ajman, Umm Al Quwain, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah. Britain ended the treaty relationships in 1971, the UAE declared independence on 2 December, and the United States recognized it the next day. The atlas start date is a mapping shortcut, not a birthday.

The first union grew from bargaining among hereditary rulers, especially the 1968 Abu Dhabi-Dubai agreement. Six emirates entered the federation on 2 December 1971; Ras Al Khaimah joined on 10 February 1972. Federal institutions took responsibility for shared affairs, but each emirate retained its own ruler and substantial local authority. “United” describes a negotiated federation, not seven old governments vanishing overnight.

The Federal National Council has 40 members. Since 2006, half have been selected through electoral colleges whose members are designated within each emirate, while rulers appoint the other half. The council reviews legislation and public policy but is consultative rather than a government-forming parliament. A 2019 directive made women half of its membership. This widened participation, but it is not universal direct national voting.

The highest constitutional authority is the Federal Supreme Council, made up of the rulers of all seven emirates. It elects the federation’s president and vice-president. On 14 May 2022 it elected Mohamed bin Zayed, ruler of Abu Dhabi, as president after the death of Khalifa bin Zayed. The modern UAE combines a federal state with seven hereditary emirate monarchies.

A short sample of official written Arabic is الإمارات العربية المتحدة دولة اتحادية مستقلة ذات سيادة. It means, “The United Arab Emirates is a federal, independent and sovereign state.” The sentence opens Article 1 of the Constitution; Article 7 names Arabic the official language. Arabic runs right to left, so the first word you see at the right edge is الإمارات, “the Emirates.” This is a modern constitutional sample, not ancient Gulf writing.

sections.title: Oil, work, trade and a spacecraft at Mars

items.text: Commercial oil exports began before federation and transformed what the new state could build. Under President Zayed, revenue financed roads, ports, electricity, clinics, schools and rapidly growing cities. Abu Dhabi held most oil resources, so federation also required bargaining over money and responsibilities. Development was spectacular but uneven across emirates, and it depended heavily on a resource whose price the country could not control.

By the World Bank’s 2021 account, non-oil activity made up roughly two-thirds of UAE output, reflecting aviation, ports, tourism, finance, construction and trade. Yet hydrocarbons still powered exports and much public revenue, leaving the economy exposed to oil-price swings. “Diversified” therefore means more engines were running; it does not mean the oil engine had been removed.

Millions of migrant workers have built, staffed and serviced the modern economy. The ILO’s UAE legal map covers who should pay recruitment costs, bans on passport confiscation, minimum working conditions, social protection, sponsorship and ways to complain. The need to map both rules and remedies is a useful warning: a protection written in law and a worker able to use it safely are not the same thing, and prosperity has not supplied equal security to every household.

The Hope probe entered Mars orbit in 2021 as the first interplanetary mission led by an Arab country. Its wide elliptical orbit lets instruments observe large portions of the Martian atmosphere on a regular cycle, connecting lower weather with gases escaping high above. By 2024 the team had published observations spanning a full Martian year. Engineers at the Mohammed Bin Rashid Space Centre built it with U.S. university partners: a national achievement assembled through international science.

sections.title: Ancient discoveries and everyday social spaces

items.text: Al Ain preserves human activity much older than the federation: Neolithic traces, circular stone tombs built around 2500 BCE and Iron Age irrigation channels called aflaj. These discoveries show long settlement and ingenious water management in an arid landscape. They belong to the deep history of territory now inside the UAE; people living thousands of years ago were not citizens of a country founded in 1971.

A majlis is a place to sit together, receive guests, share coffee and discuss family or community news. It can also host wedding congratulations or condolences. UNESCO records children accompanying adults and learning how to listen, speak politely and understand community concerns by watching elders. Women have their own majlis gatherings too, including social, literary and professional ones. Think of it as living-room hospitality mixed with a town conversation, with many local variations.

In Al Sadu weaving, women prepare wool or hair, spin thread and create strong patterned strips for tents, furnishings and camel equipment. UNESCO describes weaving gatherings as places where older women exchange family news, poems and chants. Girls traditionally begin by sorting wool, then learn spinning and increasingly difficult patterns. Modern housing and reduced pastoral life weakened the old setting, so teaching and safeguarding programmes now help keep the skill visible.

Falconry is far older and wider than the UAE, but it remains a lively family activity there. UNESCO’s nomination records experienced falconers taking children into the desert, teaching them to handle, feed and care for a bird and, most importantly, to earn its trust. The funny part is that the falcon is the athlete and the human is its chauffeur, cook, nurse and extremely patient teammate.

sections.title: School, medicine, water and the necessary toilet facts

items.text: A 2022 federal law makes education compulsory for citizen children through the end of secondary school and for resident non-citizen children through primary school. It also assigns duties to guardians and includes children with disabilities. Public schooling is free for citizens. The different compulsory endpoints are an important limitation: the same national classroom system does not create identical legal guarantees for every child living in the country.

Government-school admission rules add another difference. Citizens and eligible GCC pupils receive public places without tuition, while qualifying expatriate pupils may enter for fees, subject to academic conditions and available capacity. Many non-citizen families therefore use private schools, often with different curricula and costs. A gleaming national school system can still feel very different depending on a child’s citizenship and family budget.

The UAE’s anti-bullying programme began as a pilot in 2014. After evaluation, UNICEF reported 2024 training for 540 committee members from more than 190 Abu Dhabi schools. In surveys, 85.3 percent of staff and social workers said bullying had declined and 83 percent of students perceived safety improvements. Those are encouraging reported perceptions, not proof that every child is safe or that bullying vanished.

Children can receive the national vaccination schedule free at government facilities, from birth through grade 11, alongside newborn screening programmes. That is preventive medicine designed around a whole childhood rather than only visits after illness. As with any national programme, the schedule describes an available public service; individual children still need caregivers, appointments and follow-up to turn policy into protection.

Chronic illnesses are another side of modern health. A WHO account from 2017 described blood-pressure and blood-sugar screening in 71 primary-care clinics, multidisciplinary diabetes services and taxes intended to discourage tobacco and sugary drinks. The programme shows medicine working upstream, before a heart attack or kidney failure, while the need for it shows that wealth and hospitals do not automatically prevent diabetes and cardiovascular disease.

Official nursery standards get very specific about small bottoms: for children over two, there should be at least one child-sized toilet and one washbasin for every eight children, close to activity rooms. Diaper-changing space must be arranged hygienically away from food preparation. This is sensible engineering because a toilet too tall, too far away or too crowded is not truly a children’s toilet. The rule sets a standard; inspectors and providers still have to make it real.

WHO estimated that in 2022 about 99 percent of the population used safely managed drinking water and 98 percent used safely managed sanitation; about 95 percent of domestic wastewater was safely treated. These high national totals can hide differences in housing or work camps. They also depend on energy-intensive systems in an arid country, rather than on abundant rivers or rain.

The water system relies heavily on desalination and reuse. In 2025 the energy ministry reported more than 160 wastewater-treatment plants and reuse of 73 percent of treated water, much of it for landscaping; it set a 2036 goal of 95 percent reuse. Turning seawater into tap water and yesterday’s wastewater into irrigation water is impressive, but it costs energy and careful maintenance. A target is a homework assignment for government, not a finished grade.

ending.text: The United Arab Emirates continues as a seven-emirate federation. Its atlas lifetime is open; the last polygon interval ending in 2020 marks the end of imported geometry, not the end of the country. The genuine transition inside this record is the 1971 replacement of the Trucial treaty order by an independent federation, followed by Ras Al Khaimah’s accession in 1972. Oil-funded growth, migrant communities, federal bargaining, family traditions and public services all continue to change within that state.
